vocabulary.meaning_en: light, friendly conversation about easy topics
vocabulary.example: We made some small talk before the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: as your job, to earn money
vocabulary.note_ar: What do you do for a living? = ما عملك؟
vocabulary.note_en: What do you do for a living? = What is your job?
vocabulary.example: He drives a taxi for a living.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the type of job or industry you work in
vocabulary.example: What line of work are you in?

vocabulary.meaning_en: an activity you enjoy in your free time
vocabulary.example: My favourite hobby is hiking.

vocabulary.meaning_en: time when you are not working and can relax
vocabulary.example: What do you do in your downtime?

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) be very interested in something
vocabulary.note_ar: بعدها اسم أو فعل بـ ing
vocabulary.example: I'm really into cycling.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a style of cooking from a country or region
vocabulary.example: I love Italian cuisine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) a person who loves good food
vocabulary.example: Ask Sara about restaurants; she's a real foodie.

vocabulary.meaning_en: like a sports team and want it to win
vocabulary.example: Which team do you support?

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) liking something so much that you want to do it all the time
vocabulary.example: I watched one game and got hooked on football.

vocabulary.meaning_en: one part of a TV series
vocabulary.example: Did you see the latest episode?

vocabulary.meaning_en: what experts say the weather will be like
vocabulary.example: The forecast says it will be sunny tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: changing a lot, so you can't know what will happen
vocabulary.example: The weather here is so unpredictable.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (wind or cold) very cold and unpleasant
vocabulary.note_en: Also means a sharp, unpleasant taste.
vocabulary.example: There's a bitter wind blowing today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a little wet, in an unpleasant way
vocabulary.example: It's a cold, damp morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (weather) grey, with no sun
vocabulary.example: It was a dull day with no sun at all.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal, UK) something excellent, e.g. a great game
vocabulary.example: Last night's game was a cracker!

vocabulary.meaning_en: so interested that you cannot stop watching
vocabulary.meaning_ar: مشدود / منبهر لا يستطيع إبعاد نظره
vocabulary.example: I was riveted to my seat for the whole match.

vocabulary.meaning_en: work together with other people
vocabulary.example: I'm collaborating with the marketing team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the job you have now
vocabulary.example: How long have you been in your current role?

vocabulary.meaning_en: (UK, informal) want or would like
vocabulary.note_ar: I fancied a change = أردت التغيير
vocabulary.note_en: I fancied a change = I wanted a change.
vocabulary.example: Do you fancy a cup of tea?

vocabulary.meaning_en: say or do something to make people feel relaxed when they first meet
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يكسر الجليد / يزيل الحرج في البداية
vocabulary.example: A question about the weather is a good way to break the ice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a question that needs a longer answer, not just yes or no
vocabulary.example: "What do you enjoy about your job?" is an open question.

fine_lines.title: Open vs closed questions
fine_lines.explanation_ar: السؤال المغلق (Did you...? Are you...? Have you...?) يكون جوابه نعم أو لا فينتهي الحديث بسرعة. السؤال المفتوح (What / How / Why) يجعل الشخص الآخر يتحدث أكثر، وهذا سرّ الحديث الخفيف الناجح.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A closed question (Did you...? Are you...?) gets only yes or no. An open question (What / How / Why...) lets the other person talk more. Harry says to use open questions in small talk.

examples.sentence: What do you enjoy most about your job?

fine_lines.title: What do you do? vs What are you doing?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: What do you do (for a living)? تسأل عن المهنة. أما What are you doing? فتسأل عما تفعله الآن.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "What do you do (for a living)?" asks about your job. "What are you doing?" asks about this moment.

examples.sentence: What do you do? — I'm a nurse.
What are you doing? — I'm making tea.

fine_lines.title: It was nice meeting you vs It was nice seeing you
fine_lines.explanation_ar: meeting you لشخص تعرّفت عليه أول مرة اليوم، وseeing you لشخص تعرفه من قبل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Say "nice meeting you" to someone you met for the first time; say "nice seeing you (again)" to someone you already know.

examples.sentence: It was really nice meeting you, Mr Khan.
It was nice seeing you again, Ali.

expressions.phrase: Where are you from?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's home country or town.
expressions.example: So, where are you from?

expressions.phrase: I'm originally from ...
expressions.meaning_en: Says where you were born or grew up.
expressions.example: I'm originally from Alexandria, but I live in Cairo now.

expressions.phrase: And where are you from?
expressions.meaning_en: Returns the question after you answer it.
expressions.example: I'm from Jordan. And where are you from?

expressions.phrase: What do you do for a living?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's job.
expressions.example: What do you do for a living?

expressions.phrase: I work in the IT field. / I'm in the medical field.
expressions.meaning_ar: أعمل في مجال تقنية المعلومات / أعمل في المجال الطبي.
expressions.meaning_en: A simple, modest way to describe your job area.
expressions.example: I'm in the medical field. I work at the city hospital.

expressions.phrase: What line of work are you in?
expressions.meaning_en: Another way to ask about someone's job.
expressions.example: What line of work are you in?

expressions.phrase: Do you have any hobbies or interests?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks what someone does in their free time.
expressions.example: Do you have any hobbies or interests?

expressions.phrase: I'm really into hiking.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you like an activity a lot.
expressions.example: I'm really into hiking. I go every weekend.

expressions.phrase: I like nothing better than ...
expressions.meaning_en: Says something is your favourite thing to do.
expressions.example: I like nothing better than cycling in the park.

expressions.phrase: What about you?
expressions.meaning_en: Returns the question to the other person.
expressions.example: I love reading. What about you?

expressions.phrase: What do you do in your free time / leisure time / downtime?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about free-time activities.
expressions.example: What do you do in your downtime?

expressions.phrase: Have you seen any good movies or series recently?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل شاهدت أفلامًا أو مسلسلات جيدة مؤخرًا؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for TV or film news and recommendations.
expressions.example: Have you seen any good series recently?

expressions.phrase: You should watch it.
expressions.meaning_en: Recommends something.
expressions.example: It's a great documentary. You should watch it.

expressions.phrase: I would really recommend it.
expressions.meaning_en: Says something is very good.
expressions.example: If you haven't seen it, I would really recommend it.

expressions.phrase: What's it about?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for the story or topic of a film, book, etc.
expressions.example: I haven't seen it. What's it about?

expressions.phrase: Is there anything you think I should watch?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for a recommendation.
expressions.example: I have a free evening. Is there anything you think I should watch?

expressions.phrase: What's your favourite type of food?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about food preferences.
expressions.example: What's your favourite type of food?

expressions.phrase: What's your favourite dish / cuisine?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about a favourite meal or cooking style.
expressions.example: What's your favourite dish? Mine is mansaf.

expressions.phrase: That sounds interesting. What was it like?
expressions.meaning_en: Shows interest and asks for more details.
expressions.example: A cookery course? That sounds interesting. What was it like?

expressions.phrase: Are you into any particular sport?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks which sport someone likes.
expressions.example: Are you into any particular sport?

expressions.phrase: Which team do you support?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's favourite team.
expressions.example: You love football? Which team do you support?

expressions.phrase: How long have you been supporting that team?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks how long someone has been a fan.
expressions.example: How long have you been supporting that team? — Since I was a boy.

expressions.phrase: I just got hooked on it.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you started to love something very much.
expressions.example: My uncle took me to a match and I just got hooked on it.

expressions.phrase: I'm not really a sports fanatic.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you are not a big sports fan.
expressions.example: I'm not really a sports fanatic, but I enjoy a good game.

expressions.phrase: Did you catch the latest episode of ...?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone watched the newest part of a TV show.
expressions.example: Did you catch the latest episode of that nature series?

expressions.phrase: It's really getting exciting.
expressions.meaning_en: Says a story or show is more and more exciting.
expressions.example: Yes, I saw it. It's really getting exciting.

expressions.phrase: Have you been on any holidays recently?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone travelled recently.
expressions.example: Have you been on any holidays recently?

expressions.phrase: I'm just back from a holiday.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you returned from a trip very recently.
expressions.example: I'm just back from a holiday in Oman.

expressions.phrase: I've never been. What's it like? Would you recommend it?
expressions.meaning_ar: لم أذهب إلى هناك قط. كيف هو؟ هل تنصح به؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for someone's opinion of a place.
expressions.example: Turkey? I've never been. What's it like? Would you recommend it?

expressions.phrase: Are there any restaurants you'd recommend?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for restaurant advice, often in a new city.
expressions.example: I'm new in town. Are there any restaurants you'd recommend?

expressions.phrase: I'm a real foodie.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you love good food.
expressions.example: I'm a real foodie, so I know all the best places.

expressions.phrase: Have you tried any good restaurants lately?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about new places to eat.
expressions.example: Have you tried any good restaurants lately?

expressions.phrase: May I join you?
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask to sit at someone's table.
expressions.example: It's very busy here. May I join you?

expressions.phrase: Help yourself. / Be my guest.
expressions.meaning_en: Polite ways to say "yes, please do".
expressions.example: May I sit here? — Of course, be my guest.

expressions.phrase: Is this seat taken?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone is already using a seat.
expressions.example: Excuse me, is this seat taken?

expressions.phrase: Isn't the weather lovely today?
expressions.meaning_en: A positive comment about the weather.
expressions.example: Isn't the weather lovely today?

expressions.phrase: It's such a beautiful day.
expressions.meaning_en: A positive reply about the weather.
expressions.example: Yes, it's such a beautiful day. Let's walk after work.

expressions.phrase: Can you believe the weather? It's terrible.
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تصدّق هذا الطقس؟ إنه سيّئ جدًا.
expressions.meaning_en: A complaint about bad weather.
expressions.example: Can you believe the weather? It's terrible.

expressions.phrase: It's so unpredictable.
expressions.meaning_en: Says the weather changes all the time.
expressions.example: Sun, then rain, then sun again. It's so unpredictable.

expressions.phrase: Do you know what the forecast is for the week?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تعرف توقعات الطقس لهذا الأسبوع؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about the weather for the coming days.
expressions.example: Do you know what the forecast is for the week?

expressions.phrase: Have you heard the forecast?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone knows the weather forecast.
expressions.example: Have you heard the forecast for this weekend?

expressions.phrase: It's supposed to rain later in the week.
expressions.meaning_ar: من المفترض أن تمطر في آخر الأسبوع.
expressions.meaning_en: Reports what the forecast says.
expressions.example: It's supposed to rain later in the week.

expressions.phrase: You never know.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أحد يعلم / كل شيء ممكن.
expressions.meaning_en: Says something could change.
expressions.example: It might be sunny. You never know.

expressions.phrase: It's so miserable today.
expressions.meaning_en: Says the weather is cold, grey and wet.
expressions.example: It's so miserable today. Look at that rain!

expressions.phrase: There's a bitter wind blowing.
expressions.meaning_en: Says the wind is very cold.
expressions.example: Wear a coat. There's a bitter wind blowing.

expressions.phrase: It's a grey, damp, dull day.
expressions.meaning_en: Describes an unpleasant, cloudy, wet day.
expressions.example: It's a grey, damp, dull day. Not a day for a walk.

expressions.phrase: A day for the ducks.
expressions.meaning_en: A funny way to say it is very rainy.
expressions.example: It's pouring down. A day for the ducks!

expressions.phrase: How's the weather been treating you lately?
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly question about the weather where someone is.
expressions.example: How's the weather been treating you lately?

expressions.phrase: What's the weather like in your hometown?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about the weather where someone comes from.
expressions.example: What's the weather like in your hometown at this time of year?

expressions.phrase: How have you been?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's life since you last met.
expressions.example: Hi, Nadia! How have you been?

expressions.phrase: It's ages since I've seen you.
expressions.meaning_en: Says it has been a long time.
expressions.example: It's ages since I've seen you!

expressions.phrase: I haven't heard from you for ages.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you have had no contact for a long time.
expressions.example: I haven't heard from you for ages. How are you?

expressions.phrase: How are you getting on?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks how someone's life or work is going.
expressions.example: How are you getting on in your new job?

expressions.phrase: What have you been up to lately?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks what someone has been doing recently.
expressions.example: What have you been up to lately?

expressions.phrase: It's really kept me busy.
expressions.meaning_en: Says something took a lot of your time.
expressions.example: I changed my job, and it's really kept me busy.

expressions.phrase: Did you manage to get away for a holiday?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تمكّنت من الذهاب في إجازة؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone was able to take a holiday.
expressions.example: Did you manage to get away for a holiday last year?

expressions.phrase: How is your family doing? / How's the family?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's family.
expressions.example: How's the family? How are the kids?

expressions.phrase: Did you hear about ...?
expressions.meaning_en: Introduces news, often office news.
expressions.example: Did you hear about the new office?

expressions.phrase: It's pretty cool, isn't it?
expressions.meaning_en: Reacts positively to good news.
expressions.example: Yes, I heard about it. It's pretty cool, isn't it?

expressions.phrase: How's your day going so far?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's day.
expressions.example: Hi, Tom. How's your day going so far?

expressions.phrase: Don't ask!
expressions.meaning_en: Says things are going badly.
expressions.example: How's your day? — Don't ask! Everything went wrong.

expressions.phrase: It's been one of those days.
expressions.meaning_ar: إنه يوم من تلك الأيام السيئة.
expressions.meaning_en: Says many small things went wrong today.
expressions.example: I missed the bus and lost my keys. It's been one of those days.

expressions.phrase: Thank God it's Friday!
expressions.meaning_en: Says you are happy the work week is ending.
expressions.example: Thank God it's Friday! I'm so tired.

expressions.phrase: I can't wait for this week to be over.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أطيق انتظار انتهاء هذا الأسبوع.
expressions.meaning_en: Says the week has been hard.
expressions.example: So many meetings! I can't wait for this week to be over.

expressions.phrase: Did you catch the game last night?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone watched a match.
expressions.example: Did you catch the game last night?

expressions.phrase: Did you happen to see the game?
expressions.meaning_en: A softer way to ask if someone saw the match.
expressions.example: Did you happen to see the game on TV?

expressions.phrase: It was a cracker.
expressions.meaning_en: Says a game was excellent.
expressions.example: What a match! It was a cracker.

expressions.phrase: I was riveted to my seat.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you were too excited to look away.
expressions.example: My team was playing, so I was riveted to my seat.

expressions.phrase: Don't tell me the score.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you will watch the game later.
expressions.example: I recorded it. Don't tell me the score!

expressions.phrase: If you don't mind me saying so, I really enjoyed your presentation.
expressions.meaning_ar: إن سمحت لي بالقول، استمتعت حقًا بعرضك.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite compliment to a colleague.
expressions.example: If you don't mind me saying so, I really enjoyed your presentation.

expressions.phrase: I'm glad you found it interesting.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite reply to a compliment.
expressions.example: Thank you very much. I'm glad you found it interesting.

expressions.phrase: Are you working on any interesting projects right now?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تعمل على مشاريع مثيرة للاهتمام الآن؟
expressions.meaning_en: An open work question.
expressions.example: Are you working on any interesting projects right now?

expressions.phrase: I'm collaborating with ... on ...
expressions.meaning_en: Says who you are working with.
expressions.example: I'm collaborating with the marketing department on a new product.

expressions.phrase: Have you attended any workshops or conferences recently?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل حضرت ورش عمل أو مؤتمرات مؤخرًا؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about recent training events.
expressions.example: Have you attended any workshops recently?

expressions.phrase: What do you enjoy most about your job?
expressions.meaning_ar: ما أكثر ما تستمتع به في عملك؟
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly open question about work.
expressions.example: What do you enjoy most about your job?

expressions.phrase: How did you get started in this industry?
expressions.meaning_ar: كيف بدأت العمل في هذا المجال؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks about someone's career story.
expressions.example: How did you get started in this industry?

expressions.phrase: What made you pick this company?
expressions.meaning_ar: ما الذي جعلك تختار هذه الشركة؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks why someone chose the company.
expressions.example: What made you pick this company?

expressions.phrase: It seems to run in the family.
expressions.meaning_ar: يبدو أنه أمر متوارث في العائلة.
expressions.meaning_en: Says many family members have the same job or skill.
expressions.example: My father and brother are engineers too. It seems to run in the family.

expressions.phrase: I've been here ever since.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you have stayed since that time.
expressions.example: They offered me a job after my internship, and I've been here ever since.

expressions.phrase: How long have you been working in your current role?
expressions.meaning_ar: منذ متى تعمل في منصبك الحالي؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks how long someone has had their job.
expressions.example: How long have you been working in your current role?

expressions.phrase: I fancied a change.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you wanted something different.
expressions.example: I was in finance before, but I fancied a change.

expressions.phrase: It's been a real pleasure getting to know you.
expressions.meaning_ar: كان من دواعي سروري حقًا التعرّف إليك.
expressions.meaning_en: A warm way to end a first meeting.
expressions.example: It's been a real pleasure getting to know you.

expressions.phrase: Likewise.
expressions.meaning_en: Means "the same for me".
expressions.example: It was nice meeting you. — Likewise.

expressions.phrase: Perhaps we'll catch up again at one of these events.
expressions.meaning_ar: ربما نلتقي مجددًا في إحدى هذه الفعاليات.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you hope to meet again.
expressions.example: Perhaps we'll catch up again at one of these events.

expressions.phrase: It was nice seeing you again. Let's make sure it's not so long next time.
expressions.meaning_ar: سررت برؤيتك مجددًا. لنحرص ألا تطول المدة في المرة القادمة.
expressions.meaning_en: Ends a meeting with an old friend warmly.
expressions.example: It was nice seeing you again. Let's make sure it's not so long next time.

expressions.phrase: Let's catch up again soon.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you want to meet again soon.
expressions.example: I have to go, but let's catch up again soon.

expressions.phrase: Great catching up with you too.
expressions.meaning_ar: وأنا أيضًا سعدت بتبادل الأخبار معك.
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly reply at the end of a chat.
expressions.example: Great catching up with you too!

expressions.phrase: Let's have a coffee or a bite to eat.
expressions.meaning_en: Suggests meeting for coffee or a light meal.
expressions.example: Next time you're in town, let's have a coffee or a bite to eat.

expressions.phrase: I'd better get going now.
expressions.meaning_en: Says politely that you must leave.
expressions.example: I'd better get going now. I have a train to catch.

expressions.phrase: It was really nice talking to you.
expressions.meaning_en: Shows you enjoyed the conversation.
expressions.example: It was really nice talking to you.

expressions.phrase: Let's keep in touch.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you want to stay in contact.
expressions.example: Here's my email. Let's keep in touch.

expressions.phrase: Same here. / Same goes for me.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you feel the same.
expressions.example: I really enjoyed this. — Same here.

expressions.phrase: I'll let you get back to your day.
expressions.meaning_en: Ends a chat politely, showing you know they are busy.
expressions.example: Well, I'll let you get back to your day.

expressions.phrase: I'll see you around. Take care.
expressions.meaning_en: A casual goodbye.
expressions.example: OK, I'll see you around. Take care.

expressions.phrase: Until next time.
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly goodbye.
expressions.example: Thanks for the chat. Until next time!

expressions.phrase: Cheers, and good luck.
expressions.meaning_en: An informal British goodbye; "cheers" means thanks or goodbye.
expressions.example: Cheers, and good luck with the project.

grammar.title: Open questions with What / How / Which
grammar.explanation_ar: لكي يستمر الحديث، اسأل أسئلة مفتوحة تبدأ بـ What أو How أو Which أو Where، لأن جوابها يحتاج إلى جملة كاملة وليس نعم أو لا. ثم أعد السؤال بـ What about you?
grammar.explanation_en: To keep a chat going, ask open questions with What, How, Which or Where. They need a full answer, not yes or no. Then return the question: "What about you?"
examples: What do you enjoy most about your job?
How did you get started in this industry?

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous: How long have you been ...ing?
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have/has been + الفعل بـ ing للسؤال عن مدة شيء بدأ في الماضي وما زال مستمرًا. نجيب بـ for (مدة) أو since (نقطة بداية).
grammar.explanation_en: Use have/has been + -ing to ask about something that started in the past and is still going on. Answer with "for" (a period) or "since" (a starting point).
examples: How long have you been working in your current role?
I've been working here for six months.
I've been supporting them since I was a boy.

grammar.title: be into + noun / -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: be into عبارة غير رسمية تعني يحب أو مهتم بـ. بعدها اسم أو فعل بـ ing.
grammar.explanation_en: "Be into" is informal for "like / be interested in". Use a noun or -ing after it.
examples: Are you into any particular sport?

grammar.title: Present perfect for recent news: Have you ... recently / lately?
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم المضارع التام (have + التصريف الثالث) مع recently أو lately للسؤال عن أحداث الفترة الأخيرة.
grammar.explanation_en: Use the present perfect (have + past participle) with "recently" or "lately" to ask about recent experiences.
examples: Have you seen any good movies recently?
Have you tried any good restaurants lately?
What have you been up to lately?

questions.question: Which question asks about someone's job?
choices: What do you do for a living?
What are you up to now?
questions.explanation_ar: What do you do for a living? تسأل عن المهنة.
questions.explanation_en: "What do you do for a living?" asks about a job.

questions.question: Which is an OPEN question?
choices: What do you enjoy most about your job?
questions.explanation_ar: السؤال المفتوح يبدأ بـ What/How ويحتاج إلى جواب طويل.
questions.explanation_en: An open question (What/How...) needs more than yes or no.

questions.question: How long have you been ___ in your current role?
questions.explanation_ar: have been + الفعل بـ ing (المضارع التام المستمر).

questions.question: You are in a busy café. You want to sit at a table with one person. You say:
questions.explanation_ar: Is this seat taken? تسأل إن كان المقعد محجوزًا. أما Help yourself وBe my guest فهي ردود.
questions.explanation_en: "Is this seat taken?" is the question; "Help yourself" and "Be my guest" are replies.

questions.question: "It was a cracker!" — what does the speaker think of the game?
questions.explanation_ar: a cracker تعني شيئًا رائعًا جدًا.

questions.question: You meet an old friend after a year. Choose the best question.
choices: What do you do for a living?
What have you been up to lately?
questions.explanation_ar: What have you been up to lately? تسأل صديقًا عمّا فعله مؤخرًا.
questions.explanation_en: "What have you been up to lately?" asks a friend about recent news.

questions.question: What does "I fancied a change" mean?
choices: I wanted to do something different.
questions.explanation_ar: fancy في البريطانية تعني يرغب في.

questions.question: Which phrase ENDS a conversation politely?
choices: I'll let you get back to your day.
questions.explanation_ar: I'll let you get back to your day عبارة مهذبة لإنهاء الحديث.
questions.explanation_en: "I'll let you get back to your day" closes a chat politely.
